editorial:
Imagine starting your day in Copenhagen, looking at that famous statue by the water, only to have a talking fish tell you the real story behind it. You get swept away into an underwater world where a young mermaid turns fifteen and finally gets to see the surface. The vibe is very sweet and magical, focusing on her instant crush on a brave prince she saves from a scary storm. It feels less like a corporate movie and more like a classic fairy tale being told to you by a friend, making you really root for the mermaid as she dreams of a life on land.

What really hits home is the art style and the slow, emotional build-up of her longing for the human world. While it does not have the flashy action of modern movies, the simplicity is what makes it special. If you love old-school animation, you will find this charming, though some might find the pacing a bit slow at first.
endingExplained: The story takes a sad turn unlike the happy versions you might know. The mermaid gives up her voice to be human, but the prince marries someone else. She is told she will turn into sea foam unless she kills the prince to save herself. Because she loves him too much, she refuses to do it. She jumps into the ocean and turns into a spirit of the air, finding peace through her kindness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic fairy tales and hand-drawn art.
